elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 expressly grant licence rights to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 13.1 expressly includes contractors acting on Customer's behalf, and Section 13.2 permits contractors to support paid-up or embedded material.
Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence for software and Vendor Technology delivered on a paid-up basis perpetual.

Although Section 13.2 calls the paid-up licence irrevocable, Section 13.3 permits revocation of "a licence" for an uncured material payment or use breach and is not limited to subscription licences. The provisions therefore do not establish unqualified irrevocability for paid-up licences.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate a subscription licence only for a material breach.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 restrict revocation and suspension, but do not restrict termination and do not expressly apply a termination limitation to subscription licences.

elements.element: A material breach must remain uncured before Vendor may terminate a subscription licence.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 requires an uncured breach, notice, and a reasonable cure opportunity before revocation or suspension, but it does not impose that condition on termination of a subscription licence.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.3 expressly permit transfer to a successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates are covered upon written notice.
elements.evidence: Sections 13.1 and 13.2 provide automatic Affiliate coverage without requiring notice, which is broader than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 13.3 permits transfer to a successor in connection with a permitted assignment, a broader successor-transfer formulation that encompasses an M&A successor within the Section 24 assignment framework.

result.reason: The clause satisfies the fallback through automatic Affiliate coverage and express successor transferability. It does not satisfy the preferred position because Section 13.3 facially permits revocation of paid-up licences despite Section 13.2's irrevocability language, and the restrictions address revocation and suspension rather than termination of subscription licences. The redline preserves unrelated terms, but it is not minimal relative to the complete fallback and applies the revocation regime broadly instead of distinguishing paid-up from subscription licences.
